critique.evidence: Desktop is visually strong: the black grid, cyan/green status colors, hot-pink thesis line, restrained card borders, and curved connectors create a coherent technical aesthetic with clear hierarchy. Mobile also reflows cleanly into stacked cards and preserves readable type, spacing, and color contrast. However, the tablet viewport has a major composition failure: the navigation bar overlays and visually suppresses the first headline line, while the nav itself is clipped after the early sections. This makes the main thesis read as an obscured background element and breaks the intended hierarchy. Tablet spacing is also uneven, with the diagram stretched vertically and excessive dead space before the footer note. Across viewports, tiny uppercase metadata and footer copy are low-emphasis to the point of fragility.
critique.fix: Repair the tablet breakpoint first: place the header in normal flow or reserve its full height, collapse the long navigation into a menu, and ensure the complete headline sits unobstructed below it. Tighten the tablet diagram vertically and bring the explanatory footer closer to the content. Slightly increase the smallest metadata/footer text size and contrast while preserving the current visual system.
